content: Does anybody understand why #41507 fails at the Lint and suggest step? Here is one such failure: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/29450737658/job/87472274028
I can't see how this is related to the content of the PR (except possibly for the fact that its diff is huge). It looks like a transient error, except it's happened on 90% of the CI runs on this PR.

We were seeing similar errors earlier here: #nightly-testing-mathlib > Mathlib bump branch reminders @ 💬

Looking at the list of recent runs it seems like it might be OK now?
It was okay for a while but this fails again: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/29517475287/job/87686007236

OK, I pointed Fable at this and it seems like this is due to an issue in git 2.54.0, which will be fixed whenever github's runners get upgraded to use git 2.55 (see below).

I'm not sure when that will happen, but since this particular check doesn't block bors, I would just ignore it for now.

AI-generated details

The failure chain

  1. Every failure dies in one of the three reviewdog/action-suggester steps with:
    reviewdog: fail to get diff: failed to run git fetch: fatal: shallow file has changed since we read it
  2. Which of the three steps dies varies run to run — classic race behavior.
  3. Why only some PRs: reviewdog normally gets the PR diff from the GitHub API. When the diff is too large, the API returns 406 Not Acceptable and reviewdog logs fallback to use git command, then runs git fetch --depth=1 <repo-url> <sha> for the merge-base and head SHAs (reviewdog's diff.go). That's why the failing runs are all giant PRs — toolchain bumps, the Set refactor, mass import removals — and why they fail repeatedly on every push while ordinary PRs never hit it.
  4. Why the fetch dies: the runners currently ship git 2.54.0, which has a known shallow-handling regression (introduced by git commit 3ef68ff40e, "shallow: handling fetch relative-deepen"). It intermittently causes fatal: shallow file has changed since we read it on git fetch --depth=N into a shallow clone — exactly what reviewdog does, into the action's default depth-1 checkout. cpython is hit by the same thing (python/cpython#151365), which traces it to a git mailing-list report and to the fix (2431f5e0e5) shipped in git 2.55.0.
  5. Timeline confirms it: these failures start appearing in early June 2026, matching when runner images picked up git 2.54.0. Git 2.55 (with the fix) was released June 29 but is not yet on the runner images — today's failures still show git version 2.54.0 — and the git-core PPA also still ships 2.54.0, so you can't trivially apt-install your way out.

seems like this is happening again

Edit: it recovered
